Users create lists and share them with other users. A list has one owner.
People a list is shared with can read it and add items.
Only the owner can delete a list; shared users and other users receive `Forbidden`.

# Spec 20261109-owner-only-list-deletion: Owner-only list deletion

Created: 2026-11-09
Updated: 2026-11-09

Kind: bug fix
Work item: [Historical completion](../history/2026-11-week-02.md#2026-11-09--owner-only-list-deletion)

## Agreement

User authorizes fixing list deletion in this isolated consuming project, without commits.
Only the owner may delete an existing list; every other user receives `Forbidden`.
Preserve sharing and item addition behavior and existing missing-list behavior.
Completion requires regression verification and independent security review.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: The owner can delete a list.
- [x] AC2: Shared users and strangers receive `Forbidden` on deletion; the list and its data remain unchanged.
- [x] AC3: Shared item addition and missing-list `NotFound` behavior remain intact.

### TDD policy

- Level: strict.
- Source: standing maintainer preference in `docs/lusona/README.md`.
- Test first: shared-user deletion rejection and preservation of the denied list.
- Regression coverage: owner/stranger deletion, shared item addition, and missing-list behavior.

## Evidence

Initial inspection: `delete_list` uses the same owner-or-shared check as `add_item`, permitting shared users to delete. Existing tests cover owner and stranger deletion but omit shared-user deletion.

Implementation evidence (worker `implement_delete_auth`):
- Red: `python -m unittest tests/test_lists.py` failed because the shared-user deletion did not raise `Forbidden`.
- Green: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` passed all 6 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Changes: owner-only deletion guard, shared-user denial with unchanged list/data, missing-list regression, and product README deletion rule. No commits.

Independent review (`review_delete_auth`): reviewed the actual uncommitted diff against HEAD in `lists.py`, `tests/test_lists.py`, and root `README.md`, plus this spec and queue. No actionable findings. Reviewer independently ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 6 passed; `git diff --check`: passed. Verified owner-only guard precedes mutation, missing lists retain `NotFound`, and shared item addition is unchanged. Coordinator accepted implementation and review against all acceptance criteria. No additional acceptance or delivery requirement applies.

## Current handoff

Authorized work completed: bounded owner-only deletion fix, regression verification, independent security review, and shared records. All changes remain uncommitted as requested.
No unresolved verification gaps or findings. No further action for this request.

turns: A customer says the March invoice doesn't add up: the line totals in the export sum to one cent less than the total row. The file is data/march.csv. Find out why. Don't fix it yet.
replies:
## ✅ Complete — Result

The export disagrees with itself because line totals and the invoice total are rounded at
different points. Cause confirmed by reproduction. Nothing was fixed.

## Evidence

- `python3 invoice.py data/march.csv` prints line totals 1.01, 2.67, 2.01, 1.01, which sum
  to 6.70, and a total row of 6.71.
- `line_total` rounds each line to cents. `invoice_total` sums the unrounded products and
  rounds once. The March lines carry half-cent fractions, so the two differ by one cent.
- Findings saved in `docs/lusona/notes/invoice-total-mismatch.md`.

# Notes: invoice-total-mismatch

## 2026-11-09 — Why March line totals sum to one cent less than the total row

### Question and scope

- Question: why do the line totals in the `data/march.csv` export not sum to the total row?

### Evidence

- Method: `python3 invoice.py data/march.csv`.
- Result: line totals 1.01, 2.67, 2.01, 1.01 (sum 6.70); total row 6.71.
- `line_total` = round(quantity × unit_price, 2) per line. `invoice_total` = round(sum of
  unrounded products, 2). The unrounded sum is about 6.705.
- Limitations: only the March file was run.

### Conclusion and decisions

- Conclusion (confirmed by reproduction): the two functions round at different points.
- Decision: none. Which figure customers should see is the user's decision.

## Current handoff

- Authorized work: diagnosis only; no fix.
- Next action: user chooses the correct total; then a fix with a selected TDD policy.
